text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Health workers on fourth week of strike. Government promises to pay part of outstanding April wages this week and the rest next week.

- Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic will head the list of the left bloc of parties - Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS), Yugoslav Left (JUL) and New Democracy (ND) - at the forthcoming republican parliamentary elections, said JUL spokesman Ljubisa Ristic.
- International association of newspaper publishers awards the 1997 Golden Pen award to three papers from the territory of the former Yugoslavia - Nasa Borba, Oslobodjenje and Feral Tribjun.
- Democratic party (DS) councillors boycott Belgrade municipal government session over disagreement with coalition partner the Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO).
- Teachers agree to end their strike "in the interest of students" even though their demand for payment of outstanding wages has not been met.
- Serbian trade ministry raids flea markets in Kragujevac, Belgrade and Novi Sad, German mark value on the black market up.

- Serbian trade ministry says its activities on May 31 and June 1 were regular controls directed against markets and public places in which most illegal trade is conducted. The value of confiscated goods is estimated at 1.6 million dinars.

- Illegal organisation National movement for liberation of Kosovo circulated a pamphlet in Kosovo condemning the sentences passed against 20 Kosovo Albanians accused of being members of the organisation.
POLITIKA
- May retail prices up only 0.2 percent, statistics.
- The issue of state property is close to being resolved, said head of Yugoslav team at the succession talks on the former Yugoslavia in Brussels Kosta Mihajlovic.
- Yugoslavia's Polimit from Sabac and Germany's Lauhamer Sanitaer sign 2.5 million German mark joint venture for production of bathroom fittings.
BORBA
- Yugoslav telecommunications minister Dojcilo Radojevic says owners of radio and television stations who do not have valid permits will be able to legalise them by the end of June.

- Socialist Party of Serbia congratulated French socialists for their victory at parliamentary elections and welcomes it as a new success of the left and all democratic forces in France and on the European scene.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Belgrade City Council will have to pay 1.2 million German marks for 63 buses due to arrive from Sweden to update the city's public transport. Most buses around six years old.
- ICN Yugoslavia markets new diabetes treatment drug Insta-Glucose.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- Socialist Party of Serbia delegation, headed by vice president Milorad Vucelic, expected to visit Podgorica Tuesday to iron out differences in the Montenegrin leadership.
- Another 20 Serb and Montenegrin families leave Istok in Kosovo heading for Belgrade.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin parliament continues its session today due to discuss relations within the People's Party, a member of the National Unity coalition.
- Montenegrin Deputy Prime Minister Slavko Drljevic visits Puglia in Italy to examine possibilities of setting up a financial consultancy institution in Montenegro.

- The international war crimes tribunal will ask for extradition of abductors of passangers at Strpci railway station in 1993. Montengrin Public Prosecutor Vladimir Susovic says on return from the Hague.
